name: Sons of Uisneach

attributes.attribute: heroes of the sorrowful tale of Ulster
loved the white-skinned aller who died of grief
chief druid of Ulster who spoke the prophecy

sources: Cross, Tom Peete, and Clark Harris Slover, eds. Ancient Irish Tales. (New York: Henry Holt and Co., 1936), 239.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Sons of Uisneach are heroes of a sorrowful tale of Ireland. It begins with a prophecy by Cathbad, the chief druid of Ulster. He declared that a child born that day would be the world's most beautiful woman, but that she would bring sorrow to the province. King Concobar Mac Nessa chose to rear the child as his own. Her name was Deirdre. She grew up in the care of the wise woman Leborcham. One day Deirdre saw a raven drinking blood from the snow. She wished for a man whose hair was as black as the raven, whose lips as red as the blood, whose skin as white as the snow. Only Noísiu, the eldest son of Uisneach, was that fair. The two met and fled across Ireland to Scotland. There they lived in the wild under the protection of the region's king. But Concobar drew them back with a false promise. The Sons of Uisneach were killed, and Deirdre died of grief. She is named Deirdre of the Sorrows.
